entries.org: ACT Now Education × SANS — Veterans Day BootUp CTF
entries.what: A free 72-hour Capture the Flag cybersecurity competition over Veterans Day, run by the SANS Institute and sponsored by ACT Now Education. Built for beginner and intermediate players — no prior cyber experience needed. Top three win a SANS Skills Quest subscription.
facts: CTF registration closes Monday 9 November 2026 at 12:00 PM Eastern. No late sign-ups.
The deadline falls BEFORE the orientation webinar on Tuesday 10 November. The obvious plan — attend the webinar, then sign up — does not work. Register first, learn second.

Registering for the webinar does not enter you in the CTF. Register for the webinar first, then open your SANS account dashboard and follow the prompt to register separately for the CTF on Ranges.io. Do only the first and you will have nothing to log into on Wednesday.
Wednesday 11 November 2026 at 9:00 AM Eastern to Saturday 14 November 2026 at 9:00 AM Eastern. 72 hours, played at your own pace.

Ranked by hit rate — the fewest total attempts across the challenges you complete. Not the most flags, not the fastest finish. Speed only breaks a tie. Every wrong submission counts against you, so read the challenge and submit once rather than brute-forcing it. This is the single thing a first-timer is most likely to get wrong.
Service members, veterans, military spouses, dependents, and anyone curious about cybersecurity. Free. Virtual.
Top three by hit rate each receive a SANS Skills Quest subscription. Previous SANS BootUp CTF winners may compete but are not eligible to win a prize.

An older SANS landing page still shows a 3 November deadline and a 60-hour window ending 13 November. That page is stale. The dates here come from the SANS webcast page and the SANS press announcement, which agree with each other.

entries.what: Free monthly peer support groups for military and veteran caregivers — the person doing the caring, not the person being cared for. One hour on Zoom, facilitated by the Foundation's Mental Wellness Specialist. Three groups run, each on its own Tuesday of the month.
facts: Any military or veteran caregiver aged 18 or over whose situation matches the group topic. If you manage someone's VA appointments, track their medication, work around their bad days or hold the household together while they cannot — that is caregiving, whether or not you have ever used the word. A lot of people who qualify do not think the label applies to them.

Caring for someone with post-traumatic stress — first Tuesday of the month, 5:00 PM Eastern. Caring for someone sixty and under — second Tuesday. Caring for someone over sixty — third Tuesday. In November 2026 those fall on the 3rd, 10th and 17th.
One hour on Zoom. Free. Facilitated by Rebecca Mullaney, the Foundation's Mental Wellness Specialist. No commitment to attend every month — come when you can.

Care Groups are not mental health counselling and not therapy, and the Foundation states that on its own page rather than letting people find out in the session. Peer support sits alongside clinical care; it does not replace it.

The Foundation publishes the downsides too, which is unusual: reflecting on your own caregiving, or hearing others describe theirs, can surface difficult memories and emotions; and confidentiality is expected of everyone in the group but cannot be guaranteed. Worth knowing before you join rather than after.
Daylight saving ended 1 November 2026, so 5:00 PM Eastern that week is EST, not EDT. Your confirmation shows the start in your own time zone.
If it is heavier than that
A peer group is not crisis support. The Veterans Crisis Line is available to caregivers and family members as well as veterans: dial 988 then press 1, or text 838255.

entries.what: A free in-person resource fair run by the Disabled Veterans National Foundation, bringing together employment, housing, financial, benefits and health organisations — plus free services you can walk out with the same day. DMV area only.
facts: Monday 9 November 2026 · 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM · College Park Marriott Hotel & Conference Center, 3501 University Blvd E, Hyattsville, MD 20783. Free entry, free parking.
Two start times are published for this one: the registration page says 9:00 AM and the event graphic says 9:30 AM. Plan for 9:00 and you cannot be caught out.
A DD214 or a VA card is required. Not a description of your service — a document. Pre-registration is encouraged through the ticket page.

milConnect is the quick route but it needs a premium DS Logon; an ID.me or My HealtheVet login will not open your records there, which catches people out. A National Archives request runs one to three weeks. If you hold a VA card but not the DD214, call DVNF on 202-737-0522 before making the trip rather than finding out at the door.
Employment opportunities, housing assistance, financial assistance, veteran benefits, and physical and mental health support.

Work attire, haircuts, basic manicure, medical, dental, comfort kits, food, refreshments, gift cards and a raffle. The work attire and the haircut together amount to an interview you can actually turn up to.
Sold out. Attendee registration is still open, but an organisation hoping to exhibit has missed the window.

entries.what: A free 20-week Microsoft training programme for military spouses, toward a systems administrator role. Live and virtual. Microsoft ran a program brief on 2 November 2026 and the recording stays available, so the information is not time-locked — but the application windows are.
facts: MSSA–Military Spouse is a 20-week programme on one track: server and cloud administration, toward a systems administrator role. It covers scripting and automation, networking, identity and access management, cloud administration, and Azure and AI fundamentals.

Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM Pacific, live and virtual, with optional office hours either side. Around fifteen people to a class. This is a full-time commitment for five months, not an evening course. Anyone who works, cares for someone, or expects to move house mid-programme should work out whether those hours are possible before applying.

A LinkedIn Learning path — Networking and Administration Fundamentals, about 20 hours — is required, and it needs LinkedIn Premium. Eligible members of the military community get LinkedIn Premium free for a year, so claim that rather than paying for it. See the LinkedIn Premium entry on this list.

The programme offers role-search support and networking with corporate partners. It does not guarantee an interview with Microsoft or with a hiring partner. Worth asking what the actual placement rate is.

Microsoft's own pages disagree with each other on the application window: one place shows September 20–27 2027 for a February 2028 cohort, another shows September 20–27 2026 for the same programme. Do not plan around either. Ask Microsoft directly when the next window opens and closes.

Monday 2 November 2026, two sessions on Microsoft Teams — 12:00 PM Eastern and 4:00 PM Eastern. Session 1: aka.ms/MilSpouseSession1. Session 2: aka.ms/MilSpouseSession2. A recording is available on demand at lnkd.in/gWvVKc3d, so the brief itself is not a deadline.

The separate MSSA programme for transitioning service members, veterans and retirees is open to all US and UK MoD branches. Active duty applicants need a separation date within 180 days of the programme start and must speak to their local SkillBridge manager first.

entries.what: Ten paid subscriptions the military community can use at no cost through the Morale, Welfare and Recreation digital library — O'Reilly Learning, EBSCO LearningExpress, Tutor.com, Universal Class, Mango Languages, Libby/OverDrive, The Wall Street Journal, Consumer Reports, Ancestry Library Edition and Gale OneFile: Vocations and Careers. One login covers all of them.
facts: Under DoD Instruction 1015.10: active duty; Reserve and National Guard; retirees; Medal of Honor recipients; veterans with a 100% service-connected disability; and eligible dependents with an ID card.

A veteran rated below 100% service-connected does not get access on veteran status by itself. This is the same rule that governs on-base MWR privileges, not a decision the library makes. Worth knowing before you create an account.

DoD and Coast Guard civilians, both appropriated and non-appropriated fund, qualify while stationed outside the United States. Stateside, access depends on the individual resource. Local nationals sign in with a library card number; contractors have to go through the Contact Us link.

Go to dodmwrlibraries.org and pick your service's portal, then sign in with your DoD ID number and date of birth. Not a CAC and not a DS Logon — the portal checks you against DEERS. Then open Digital Collections, A to Z.

If your ID card shows an SSN instead of a DoD ID number, enter 0000000000 in the DoD ID field and then the last four digits of your SSN on the next page. This is published on their own FAQ and almost nobody repeats it. It is the step that stops older retirees getting in.

O'Reilly Learning carries technology, AI, cybersecurity and certification prep — the full library, not a sampler. If you are studying Security+, AWS or Azure, look there before buying a course. EBSCO LearningExpress carries the practice tests people usually pay for separately.

Consumer Reports is blocked by some military network filters, and single sign-on resources can fail on military or high-security networks. Try from a personal connection before concluding you do not have access. Offline reading works for most but not all magazines, e-books and audiobooks.

Tutor.com appears in this collection but carries its own eligibility rules on top of the library's. There is also a separate, directly funded route at military.tutor.com — see the Tutor.com entry on this list, which has different rules again.

Which resources appear differs by service portal and changes over time. If something listed here is missing from your A to Z, check another service portal or ask your MWR library before assuming it has gone.

entries.what: Heroes Sail Free — $0 base cruise fare for the first two guests in an interior stateroom on Margaritaville at Sea Islander or Paradise, for verified GOVX members. A separate offer takes 20% off retail for guests one through four.
facts: Active and former U.S. military, plus first responders, educators, medical personnel and government employees. You must be a verified GOVX member at the time of booking.
$0 cruise fare for the first and second guests only, in an interior stateroom on Islander or Paradise. Third and fourth guests pay prevailing retail rates. There is no single-traveller offer.
Auto-assigned “We Pick” staterooms only — you do not choose the room. Capacity-controlled, select sail dates, first come first served.
Taxes, fees and port expenses are assessed per guest and are due at booking, plus gratuities and onboard charges. A free fare is not a free invoice.
Distinct from the free cabin: 20% off the retail fare for guests one through four. Does not apply to single travellers, and blackout dates may apply based on stateroom availability.

entries.what: All-expenses-paid vacations for severely combat-wounded service members — medically retired, former or active — and their immediate family. Nominations are accepted year-round and reviewed quarterly.
facts: Generally a combined disability rating of 80–100% or greater, with a single physical disability rating of 30% or more, for injuries or wounds sustained during combat.

Blindness or loss of vision; severe burns; spinal cord injury or paralysis; traumatic brain injury; or loss of one limb, arm or leg, or more. This list is the real gate — the rating alone does not decide it.
The organization describes the trips as all-expenses-paid but does not itemise what that includes anywhere on its site. Ask for the list in writing before you plan a week around it.

Anyone may nominate. Referrals come from past recipients, VA personnel and active-duty personnel, as well as direct contact. The nominee completes the V4W application. New vacations are considered quarterly.
The organization states plainly that there are far more candidates than available vacations, and that no application is guaranteed a trip.

entries.what: Sponsored restorative getaways for military members, veterans, first responders and Gold Star families. Applications are open year-round and the board of directors makes the final selection.
facts: Four eligibility categories on the application: Military, Veteran, First Responder, and Gold Star Family. Verification may require service records, a veteran ID, first responder credentials or Gold Star documentation.

Individual review, then verification of service and eligibility, then a recommendation from an Application Review Committee, then a final decision by the board of directors weighed on mission, funding, capacity and expected restorative impact.
The organization states its getaways are intended to complement, not replace, professional medical or mental health treatment. Worth knowing before you apply on someone else's behalf.
Trip format, how many family members are included, and whether transportation is covered are not stated on the application page. Ask before making any plans.

entries.what: Seven donated nights in a condominium, typically Orange Beach or Gulf Shores, Alabama, or northwest Florida, for veterans who deployed to a combat zone after 9/11 and their families. Trips run in spring and fall.
facts: Served in the United States military, any branch and any rank, and deployed to a combat zone on or after 11 September 2001.
Seven nights in a property donated by owners and rental management companies, typically coastal Alabama — Orange Beach or Gulf Shores — or northwest Florida, in spring or fall.
The most recent returning deployers, within 12 months, always have priority. Registering first does not guarantee selection.
The organization may offer gas cards, gift certificates for necessities or meals so that money does not stop a family coming. It is not advertised — ask when you register.
The live registration form is still labelled 2025 and the page states no open or close date. Confirm the current intake with the organization before counting on a trip.

entries.what: A two-night family condominium weekend at St. James, North Carolina, with meals, gas money and a family photo session, for active-duty families. The 2027 application window opens 1 December 2026.
facts: Active-duty service members and their families, any branch and any location. Veterans are not listed. The weekend is for military members, spouses and their children — other relatives and friends are not covered.

Two nights in a two- or three-bedroom condominium at St. James, near Southport and Oak Island. Friday dinner and both breakfasts prepared and in the condo on arrival, restaurant coupons for two lunches and Saturday dinner, money for gas to drive there, a family photo session, gifts and one Saturday activity.
Applications for 2027 begin 1 December 2026. The organization contacts applicant families from 1 January 2027 to schedule. No closing date is published.

Not first come first served. First priority goes to personnel separated from their families and recently deployed to a combat zone or similar area; selections are then based on rank and deployment length.
The rental condominiums cannot accommodate pets, and weekend parking or storage for boats and trailers is not available.

entries.what: Six-day therapeutic retreats, Friday to Wednesday, for military and veteran families and couples — all branches including Coast Guard, all eras, Guard and Reserve and first responders included. Lodging, meals and activities are covered; travel is not.
facts: Active duty, retirees, veterans, Reserve and Guard, and first responders; all branches including Coast Guard, all eras. For families and couples — space is limited to immediate family or the one person who supports you. Solo attendees are referred to partner organizations.
Six days, Friday to Wednesday. Your own cabin, lodge room or duplex with linens and towels, all meals, activities and equipment such as helmets, and professional family portraits.

A $100 commitment fee by PayPal secures your retreat date. It is refunded on successful completion of the entire six-day retreat, and the wrap-up survey must be submitted before you leave the retreat centre on the last day.

Cancel less than one month before your retreat date and the $100 is forfeited, you must wait two years before reapplying, and a $200 commitment fee is then required. This is published and almost nobody repeats it.

Transportation to and from the retreat, souvenirs and personal items. Locations are remote and rideshare is not recommended. Families with financial need can work with the intake coordinator on getting there.
All classes and workshops are mandatory. Recreation activities are optional.

entries.org: Red, White & Blue Summit — Hampton Roads, Fall 2026
entries.what: Three free in-person events in Norfolk on 18 and 19 November for service members, veterans, military spouses and families, run by the Center for Military and Family Advancement, part of the Hampton Roads Workforce Council. Thursday is the hiring day — meet employers in the morning, fifteen-minute interviews the same afternoon.
facts: 9:30 AM to 1:30 PM EST at Vista Point Conference Center, 1754 Massey Hughes Drive, Norfolk. Schools, childcare, housing, benefits, SkillBridge, apprenticeship pathways, training and certifications.

5:30 to 8:00 PM EST at Waters Edge Winery, 6464 Hampton Blvd, Norfolk. Off base, so no gate to clear. No childcare provided. Eventbrite lists it as “Red, White & Brew (Fall Edition) Southside” — search that exact name or the ticket will not come up.

9:00 AM to 3:00 PM EST at Vista Point. Employers on the floor 9 to 12, fifteen-minute interviews 1 to 3. Free professional headshots, résumé and profile help, and SKYBOX one-to-one mentoring for E-7 to O-6 and experienced military spouses. Children welcome.

Vista Point sits inside Naval Station Norfolk, so both daytime events are on base. Without a DoD ID, Navy Region Mid-Atlantic requires a REAL ID-compliant driver's licence, state ID card or US passport, plus the SECNAV 5512/1 base access registration form, plus a pass from the Pass & ID office.

Naval Station Norfolk suspended its Trusted Traveler Program in March 2026, so someone holding a CAC can no longer vouch for passengers in their vehicle. Visitors need a sponsor and a valid visitor pass. That is the most recent published policy as of this check.

The organizer has not published a gate-access process for this event, and they may well have one arranged. Call the Center for Military and Family Advancement on 757-807-0423 and ask, days ahead — not on the morning of the 19th.

45+ organizations scheduled for the 19th. Named so far: General Dynamics Mission Systems, HII Mission Technologies, Newport News Shipbuilding, Norfolk Naval Shipyard, Dominion Energy, USAA, Fiserv, Epsilon Systems Solutions, Wawa, City of Norfolk, City of Virginia Beach, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
Each event has its own Eventbrite ticket — register for every one you plan to attend. All three are free. This is the fall edition of a quarterly series that ran previously as the 757 Career Summit.

entries.org: Google Launchpad for Veterans — Gen AI Leader 2026
entries.what: A free two-day virtual Google Cloud Gen AI Leader training on 12 and 13 November 2026, hosted by ROI Training, ending in a complimentary certification exam voucher. Open to U.S. and Canada military veterans and service members. Registration needs the access code ACTNowEducation.
facts: U.S. and Canada military veterans and service members. No prior technical experience is required — Gen AI Leader is the non-technical track.

12 and 13 November 2026, virtual, hosted by ROI Training. Interactive training sessions plus a panel discussion with veterans from Google. Start times and the time zone are not stated on the published material.
Two days of training, a complimentary Gen AI Leader exam voucher, two follow-on exam prep sessions, and a chance at a pair of Google socks — in 2025 the socks went to the first 500 people who passed.

Register with ACTNowEducation. The published steps are: click Sign Me Up, select “Continue without email”, enter your email address, enter the access code, then finish the remaining prompts. Steps two and three look contradictory and are meant to be followed in that order.

Attending earns a voucher, not a certification. The Gen AI Leader exam is booked and sat separately, and passing it is what earns the credential. A voucher left unredeemed is the most common way this ends in nothing.

The exam prep session dates and the voucher expiry date are not on the flyer or on anything Google has published for the 2026 cohort. Ask for both at registration and diary the expiry the day the voucher lands.

2024 ran as Cloud Digital Leader. In 2025 the event was 13–14 November, prep sessions were 17 and 21 November, and Google encouraged taking the exam between 21 November and 19 December without publishing a voucher expiry. Useful as a shape for what to expect, not as 2026 dates.

entries.what: 82 restaurants appear on the Veterans Day lists circulating this year. 28 were confirmed when ACT Now Education compiled its guide on 29 October; 15 more were reported by deal trackers without chain confirmation, and 39 gave free food in 2025 with no 2026 terms announced. Re-checked against VA News and Military.com on 8 November.
facts: 28 chains as of the guide's compilation date: Applebee's, Bob Evans, Chili's, Cotton Patch Cafe, Denny's, Golden Corral, Hoss's, In-N-Out, Lazy Dog, Mission BBQ, Olive Garden, Pilot/Flying J, Red Robin, Sheetz, Sizzler, Texas Roadhouse, White Castle, IHOP, Cracker Barrel, Bonefish Grill, Outback, Starbucks, Krispy Kreme, Dunkin', 151 Coffee, Marzoni's, Chipotle and Rubio's.
VA News has since confirmed eight more: Red Lobster, Shake Shack, Yard House, Smashburger, Freddy's, Bar Louie, Biscuit Belly and World of Beer. Any list dated late October is already behind.
Veterans Canteen Service at VA medical centers runs on the 10th, a day before Veterans Day. Worth knowing if you have an appointment that Tuesday.
A voucher, not a meal on the day. Collected between 11 AM and 2 PM on the 11th and redeemed on a later visit, good through 31 May 2027. Confirmed on Military.com.
Denny's runs 5 AM to noon. Sizzler until 4 PM. Golden Corral does not start until 4 PM. Outback covers both the 10th and the 11th. Hoss's $10-off-$40 voucher is good to 25 November.
Not all of it is free
Chipotle needs a $5 purchase. Rubio's is buy-one-get-one with code VETS26. Drinks, tax and tip are usually not included anywhere, and franchises can opt out of the whole thing.
Military ID, VA card, DD-214, or the veteran designation on a driver's licence. Most offers are dine-in at participating locations. Starbucks includes spouses; most do not.
The guide states the free meal is for the service member and that family pays. Neither VA News nor Military.com says that. Ask when you call rather than assuming either way.
A chain confirming nationally does not bind the branch near you. One phone call beats a wasted drive, and it is the only step that makes any of this reliable.

entries.org: Service to Success — Virtual Military & Federal Hiring Fair
entries.what: A free three-hour virtual hiring fair on Friday 13 November 2026, 3:00 to 6:00 PM EST, run by Service to Success with ACT Now Education and hosted on Zoom Events. For veterans, transitioning service members, military spouses, SkillBridge candidates and the federal community.
facts: 3:00 to 6:00 PM EST — 2 PM CT, 1 PM MT, noon PT. Three hours, not a drop-in. The intro keynote runs 3 to 4 PM and the registration page says to join there first; a help chat runs 4 to 6 PM alongside the fair.

The full event name is the Virtual Military AND Federal Hiring Fair. Most graphics drop the federal half. Open to veterans, transitioning service members, military spouses, SkillBridge candidates and the federal community.

Amazon, Navy Federal Credit Union, ManTech, V2X, T-Mobile, TEKsystems, CHRISTUS Health, Leaf Home, ARA, FDM Group, and GuidePoint Security — the last of which is named on the registration page and on none of the circulating graphics.

The organiser states companies are still signing up and that the final list of registered employers is emailed to attendees before the day. Do not skip the event because your industry is missing from a flyer.
IT and cybersecurity; engineering and defense; healthcare; operations, finance and sales.

The servicetosuccess.com/HiringFair link redirects to Zoom Events, not to their own site. Register with a Zoom account or with an email address. Free. Zoom restricts registration to a listed set of countries, which may matter if you are OCONUS.
The confirmation email arrives immediately after registering and is the one that carries the final employer list. The organiser flags that it often lands in spam.
What to ask on the day
Which of your roles fit what I have done; what am I missing to qualify; what should I do next to apply. A conversation gives you the gap analysis an application never will.

entries.org: ACT Now Education — SkillBridge: three tech roles
entries.what: Three open DoD SkillBridge placements sourced by ACT Now Education, for transitioning service members in their final 180 days of service: Site IT Support Technician (Flowery Branch, GA), Network Test Lab Engineer (Roseville, CA hybrid or Andover, MA), and Junior Data Engineer (Cincinnati, OH). Applications are by email, rolling, with no posted closing date.
facts: Site IT Support Technician — Flowery Branch, GA. Network Test Lab Engineer — Roseville, CA (hybrid) or Andover, MA. Junior Data Engineer — Cincinnati, OH.

The Department of Defense remains responsible for all pay and benefits for the duration of the placement, and the industry partner receives the participant at no cost. Any hourly or annual figure attached to one of these roles is the job's own rate, applicable if and when the placement converts to employment — not compensation during the 180 days. Only the Junior Data Engineer listing labels its figure correctly, as "after SkillBridge." Ask when the listed rate starts before accepting.

SkillBridge sits inside the final 180 days of service. It is not open to someone 6 to 12 months out, who can plan and apply but cannot yet participate. Participation must also occur within 180 days of discharge.

180 continuous days of active duty already served. Approval from the first field grade commander with Article 15 authority. Open to all four branches plus the Guard and Reserve on qualifying active-duty orders.
A placement more than 50 miles from the service member's duty station requires specific commander authorisation. All three of these roles are tied to a named city, so this applies to most applicants.
Industry partners generally cannot provide gifts or compensation, but may offer subsistence, lodging or travel subsidies where these are offered to all similar trainees.
Email nicole.dhanraj@actnoweducation.org with the job title and your location preference. Rolling, no posted deadline.

When does the listed rate start — during the placement or only on conversion? Is there a conversion offer at the end, and what has the conversion rate been? Will the host support a placement more than 50 miles from the duty station?

entries.org: Wounded Warrior Project × USAA — Warrior Secure Start
entries.what: A $1,000 financial empowerment grant for veterans in their first 24 months after military service, run by Wounded Warrior Project with USAA funding. Complete a financial education course with a WWP Financial Readiness specialist, submit the certificate, and the grant is paid into your bank account. Nothing to repay. Registration with WWP is free and is the prerequisite.
facts: The common assumption that WWP is only for the visibly wounded is the main barrier to this grant. WWP's registration page states that a visible injury or combat-related injury is not required, and sets eligibility at having served on or after 11 September 2001.

Veterans who served on or after 11 September 2001; active-duty service members; service members preparing to transition; eligible National Guard and Reserve members; and family members, caregivers and others in a warrior's support system. Registration is free.

You can join WWP while still serving or while preparing to transition. Because the grant window is the first 24 months after service, registering early means the window is spent using the program rather than joining it.

$1,000, one time, described by USAA as purpose-built for veterans during the first 24 months after military service. Announced 9 July 2026 as part of a $5M, five-year USAA commitment expected to support more than 4,000 veterans.

Paid directly into the veteran's bank account after the financial education course is completed and the certificate is submitted. Usable for emergency savings, paying down debt, or another financial goal. No repayment.

Not a self-serve form. The veteran meets a WWP Financial Readiness specialist who reviews their situation before directing them to the course modules. The program is aimed at veterans experiencing financial strain, and grants run in the hundreds per year rather than unlimited.

An 80% quiz pass mark, two coaching sessions and a 60-day completion window circulate with this program but appear on neither USAA's announcement nor WWP's Financial Readiness page, which does not name Warrior Secure Start at all. One published account describes course modules with three classes. Confirm actual requirements with the specialist at enrollment.
Register at woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/wwp-registration, or call 888.WWP.ALUM (888.997.2586). The WWP Resource Center can confirm which documents are needed and answer eligibility questions.

entries.what: A recruiting platform that translates military records into scored corporate competencies and routes veterans to employers' hard-to-fill roles. Free for veterans; employers are the paying customers. Also an authorized DoD SkillBridge industry partner that manages the MOU, training plan and compliance on the employer's behalf, so some roles can be entered through SkillBridge rather than as a direct hire.
facts: Headlamp does not hire you itself. It verifies what you did in service and routes you to a client employer with a role to fill. The practical consequence: the recruiter reading your message is paid to place you, not to screen you out, which is the opposite of an applicant tracking system.
Veterans and service members use it at no cost. Employers pay for access, which is why the veteran side carries no fee or subscription.

Headlamp states it is an authorized DoD SkillBridge industry partner and handles the Memorandum of Understanding, training plans and OFCCP compliance for the host employer. Anyone inside their final 180 days of service should ask whether a given role can be entered on SkillBridge, where the DoD continues to pay the service member and the host pays nothing. This is not stated on the individual role postings.

Ten listings, eleven seats. Butte, MT onsite: Director of Marketing, Sr Mechanical Engineer, Entry-Level Mechanical Engineer, Sr Chemical Engineer, Process Development Engineer, Controls Engineer, Sr Electromechanical Engineer, Outside Sales Engineer (2 seats). Latrobe, PA onsite: Inside Sales Rep. Remote: Outside Sales Rep. Expect this list to change.

The remote Outside Sales Rep lists twelve hub cities (Houston, Dallas, Denver, Phoenix, Atlanta, Salt Lake City, Reno, Las Vegas, Charlotte, Indianapolis, Columbus, Midland/Odessa). Confirm whether that means field sales based near a hub or genuinely location-independent work.
Most roles are in one place
Eight of the ten current listings are onsite in Butte, Montana. For most applicants that is a relocation decision rather than a commute, and it is worth settling before investing in an application.

Contact is via the recruiter rather than a job board. Send the role, your location and one specific example — name the equipment, the fault and the fix, so the recruiter can repeat it to a hiring manager without a follow-up question.
myheadlamp.com for the platform and veteran access. Current roles run through recruiter Lora Kelly at linkedin.com/in/lorakelly. General enquiries: info@myheadlamp.com.

entries.org: ACT Now Education — free certification directory
entries.what: A directory of funded certification programs for veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses, covering CompTIA, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Cisco, ISC2, PMI, Splunk, IBM and more. Eleven programs listed on the veteran side and ten on the spouse side.
facts: Act Now Education, IVMF Onward to Opportunity, VetsInTech, Per Scholas, NPower, ServiceNow, Purdue University Northwest, Boots to Books, SANS Cyber Workforce Academy, Cloud Veterans, MedCerts.

Act Now Education, IVMF Onward to Opportunity, VetsInTech, Per Scholas, NPower, Cloud Veterans, SANS Cyber Workforce Academy, Boots to Books, SpouseWorks Scholarship, MedCerts. CISSP appears on the spouse list but not the veteran one.

ServiceNow and Purdue University Northwest appear on the veteran side only. ServiceNow's link is a SkillBridge URL, so it is for the final 180 days of service rather than for veterans already separated.
MedCerts is a paid school that accepts funding such as SpouseWorks rather than a no-cost program. Price it before committing.
ACT Now runs a live Weekly Rundown on Saturdays at 1 PM Eastern at actnoweducation.org/weekly-rundown for walking through these.

entries.what: Up to $4,000 in Department of Defense funding for a military spouse to earn a license, certification or associate degree, or to keep an existing credential current. Renamed from MyCAA, and the rank restriction was removed on 27 July 2026.
facts: Before 27 July 2026 eligibility was limited to spouses of junior pay grades. The Office of Spouse Employment: eligibility was limited by rank before that date, and as of that date there is no rank eligibility restriction. Spouses turned down under the old rule qualify now.

Spouses of active-duty Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force and Space Force members regardless of rank or pay grade, plus spouses of Guard and Reserve members on qualifying Title 10 orders. High school or GED required. Employed spouses are eligible.

A spouse who is themselves on Title 10 orders; a spouse legally separated or under court order from a Title 10 member; a spouse whose Guard or Reserve sponsor is in warning/alert, post-deployment, demobilization or transition status.
Maximum $4,000 total but no more than $2,000 per government fiscal year (1 October to 30 September), counted by the course start date rather than the application date.

Unused funds are forfeited three years after the first course starts. Using $500 in year one and $500 in year two means the remaining $1,000 cannot be recovered. Reaching the full $4,000 requires planning across fiscal years from the outset.
Tuition toward a license, certification or associate degree, continuing education to maintain a credential, national tests including CLEP, and the certification exam itself. Not taxable.

Bachelor's or higher coursework, certificates of completion that do not lead to a certification or license, books, supplies, computers, fees of any kind including registration and technology fees, reimbursements, courses already started, repeat courses, high school or GED completion, ESL, transport, lodging or childcare.

A school-completed Education and Training Plan must be approved before any funding request, and review takes up to 14 business days. Paperwork must be approved before the sponsor's separation or release from Title 10 orders. Associate degrees must finish within 12 months, licenses and certificates within 18, with no exceptions.
The process begins with a SpouseWorks career coach via Military OneSource on 800-342-9647, not with an online form. Login moved from DS Logon to myAuth.

entries.what: Free, fully online professional certification training from Syracuse University's Institute for Veterans and Military Families, covering AWS, CompTIA, Cisco, PMI, Six Sigma, HR and Python credentials. Course enrollment, materials and advising are free to every participant.
facts: The program funds a single certification exam, and eligible candidates may participate only once. More than one course can be taken, one at a time, but the funded exam is singular. Choose the credential before enrolling.
Active-duty members are covered during their final six months. Veterans and spouses are covered only while currently unemployed. Employed Guard and Reserve members pay their own exam fee.

Active duty transitioning within 6 months; any veteran with at least 180 days of service and an honorable discharge, with no time limit after separation; spouses of active duty, eligible veterans, Guard and Reserve; and part-time Guard and Reserve members.
Roughly 6 to 8 hours a week over 90 days, delivered fully online and self-paced, with installation-based options also available. The first course must finish within 90 days of the cohort start.
Online-only applicants face a 2 to 3 month wait for a future cohort, so apply well before the credential is needed.

entries.what: A competitive, aptitude-based scholarship delivering GIAC certifications — GFACT, GSEC and GCIH — at no cost to the participant. Designed as a career entry route into cybersecurity rather than an upskilling program.
facts: Prior or current work experience in cybersecurity or information security makes an applicant ineligible. So does already holding a GIAC certification, or a graduate degree in the field. It is built for career changers, which is the opposite of what most applicants assume.

Described in the program's own application guide as a competitive, aptitude-based scholarship where participation is earned through merit. Applicants sit an online aptitude assessment and are not shown their score; an invitation to complete the application is not an offer.
US citizens and lawful permanent residents only. Active-duty applicants must be within 6 months of separation. Current full-time students are not eligible. An undergraduate degree is fine.
GFACT for foundations, GSEC for security essentials and GCIH for incident handling — three GIAC certifications at no cost to the participant.

entries.what: Free tuition-free technology training toward A+, Google IT Support, CySA+, AWS Cloud Practitioner and Salesforce Administrator, delivered at campuses across the US with a dedicated military-connected track.
facts: Civilian applicants need individual or household income below 80% of the campus-based Area Median Income. Veterans, active duty, Reserve, Guard and military spouses are eligible with income below $200,000, so most military-connected applicants who assume they earn too much do not.

Current employment counts current income. Unemployed up to 90 days counts the last job's income; unemployed beyond 90 days counts as zero. Household income covers everyone in the residence over the last 12 months. Savings, benefits, passive income, child support and inheritance are excluded.
Training runs through named campuses including Dallas, Atlanta, National Capital Region, Los Angeles, Pittsburgh and New York. Check the campus list before planning around it.

entries.what: No-cost technology training toward ITIL, A+, Security+, AWS Cloud, AWS Solutions Architect Associate and the Google IT Support certificate, with a dedicated track for veterans and military spouses.
facts: Free of charge, not of time

Most classes require a four-hour-a-day commitment Monday through Friday for up to 20 weeks, plus roughly two more hours daily of outside work. That is not something that fits around full-time employment.

Veterans and military spouses over 21 — no upper age limit and no stated education requirement — who are transitioning through DoD SkillBridge, honorably discharged, Guard or Reserve, or a military spouse. The young adult track is 18 to 26 with a high school diploma.
Applicants must be in or near NPower's listed cities. Online courses are offered only within that geographic footprint, so remote attendance from outside it is not available.
Fully no-cost to selected participants with no debt on completion. No stipend is offered.

entries.what: Amazon's military talent acquisition routes for veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses: a landing page, cleared roles, Pathways, two apprenticeships, Hiring Our Heroes fellowships, data center roles, a skills translator, a webinar series, job simulations, Amazon Leo and Reliability Maintenance Engineering.
facts: 1  Military landing page = https://www.amazon.jobs/military; 2  Cleared roles = https://amazon.jobs/content/en/cleared-talent; 3  Pathways (Operations) = https://amazon.jobs/content/en/career-programs/pathways; 4a Tech apprenticeship = https://www.amazon.jobs/en/landing_pages/mil-apprentice; 4b RME apprenticeship = https://www.amazon.jobs/en/landing_pages/rme-apprentice; 5  Fellowships (HOH) = https://www.hiringourheroes.org/career-services/fellowships/; 6  Data center roles = https://amazon.jobs/content/en/teams/amazon-web-services/data-centers; 7  Military Skills Translator = https://amazon.oplign.com/; 8  Military Webinar Series = https://www.amazon.jobs/military  [same as #1]; 9  Job simulation = https://app.redeployable.io/join; 10 Amazon Leo = https://amazon.jobs/content/en/teams/devices-services/leo; 11 Reliability Maint. Eng. = https://amazon.jobs/content/en/teams/amazon-operations  [general Operations]

Re-decoded 24 November, nine days after the first check, same result. #8 Military Webinar Series resolves to the general military landing page, identical to #1, not to anything webinar-specific. #11 Reliability Maintenance Engineering resolves to the general Amazon Operations team page, not to RME; the RME apprenticeship link at #4b is the more direct route. One of the two Job Simulations codes would not decode from the circulated image.

Data center roles are advertised as many not requiring a college degree. Both apprenticeships are built to supply the skills. Military Pathways lists an engineering bachelor's as preferred rather than required.
The job simulations let a candidate run an Amazon Operations Manager role before submitting an application. Free, and there are two separate simulations rather than one.
Military Apprentice and RME Apprentice are separate tracks with separate pages, presented under a single heading on the source material.

The webinar series and the main landing page resolve to the same URL, so the webinar route does not reach a webinar listing. The Reliability Maintenance Engineering route resolves to the general Amazon Operations team page rather than an RME-specific one.

The skills translator runs on amazon.oplign.com and the job simulations on app.redeployable.io — neither is an Amazon domain. The simulation links carry campaign tracking parameters that may not persist.
amazon.jobs/military — also where the webinar series route leads.
Skills translator: amazon.oplign.com. Job simulations: app.redeployable.io/join. Fellowships run through Hiring Our Heroes at hiringourheroes.org/career-services/fellowships.
Pathways: amazon.jobs/content/en/career-programs/pathways. Amazon Leo: amazon.jobs/content/en/teams/devices-services/leo. Operations and RME: amazon.jobs/content/en/teams/amazon-operations.

entries.org: Amazon Military Pathways — officer leadership track
entries.what: A three-year operations leadership development program entering as an Operations Manager at an Amazon operations facility, progressing through Area Manager to Senior Operations Manager. Listed on Amazon's military material as Pathways, which is easy to mistake for an MBA-only route.
facts: A bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline is listed as preferred, not required, and the posting does not ask for an MBA. The MBA framing on circulating material turns away candidates who already meet the stated qualifications.
The basic qualifications specify a commissioned officer at the company-grade level. No enlisted route appears on the posting.
Basic qualifications state transitioned or retired within one year, marked no exceptions. The window runs from each person's own separation date rather than a programme closing date.
Approximately ten years of active duty service, plus experience leading teams in operational or logistics environments.

Service academy graduates; operations, logistics, supply chain or engineering specialties; battalion or company-level command or equivalent leadership of 100 or more personnel; complex logistics or transportation management experience.

The 2027 posting lists a starting salary of $147,100. Placement is matched to a US operations facility through a recruiter before an offer, and candidates must be willing to relocate at hire. Cohorts start between January and July.
The apprenticeships, data center roles and cleared roles remain open without officer status, service length or a separation window, and none of them require a degree.

entries.org: HHS — Beyond the Uniform: federal hiring webinar
entries.what: A free one-hour webinar on getting hired into federal service, open to anyone with no eligibility gate and no proof of service: navigating USAJOBS, veteran and military spouse hiring authorities, federal résumé construction, application and assessment guidance, interview preparation, and a live Q&A.
facts: The circulating material never names the host. The USAJOBS federal events calendar lists this session for 17 November under 'Connecting Veterans & Military Spouses-Public Service Opportunities', hosted by the Department of Health and Human Services and carrying the flyer's exact subtitle. HHS sits above CDC, FDA, NIH, CMS, the Indian Health Service and HRSA, so the hiring authorities covered are ones they use daily across far more than clinical roles.
Tuesday 17 November 2026, 2:00 to 3:00 PM Eastern, online, free.

Browser attendees get no Q&A box. On a session whose value is asking a federal hiring specialist what you are doing wrong, that is the difference between attending and watching. Install the Teams app before the start time.
Open to anyone. No proof of service, no spouse ID, no separation window.

Four federal hiring events ran on 17 November alone, with Interior on the 18th and both IRS and the DoD SpouseWorks virtual hiring fair on the 19th. See the USAJOBS events entry — the calendar outlasts any one session.

entries.what: The federal government's own calendar of free hiring events, run by the agencies themselves rather than by third parties: USAJOBS walkthroughs, federal résumé and assessment sessions, veteran and military spouse hiring-authority briefings, and agency virtual hiring fairs. 29 events were listed live on the day of the check.
facts: No registration fee on any listing. Most run one hour online, with a live Q&A, and several each week are veteran- or military spouse-specific.

Listings come from the agencies and DoD programs directly — HHS, VA, FDA, FAA, Interior, IRS and the DoD SpouseWorks hiring fairs all appeared in a single week — so the hiring authorities explained are the ones that office uses.

The calendar can be filtered, and veteran and military spouse sessions are labelled. Each listing carries its own registration link and its host agency, which is often the detail missing from material circulating about the same event.
Any single webinar expires within days. This calendar does not, and it is where the next one appears. Bookmark the calendar rather than the session.
Agencies run the same briefings on a cycle, so missing one is not losing the information — check the calendar for the next instance rather than waiting a year.

entries.org: USDA-APHIS — Moore Air Base hiring fair (McAllen, TX)
entries.what: A three-day walk-in hiring fair for the New World Screwworm Sterile Fly Production Facility at Moore Air Base, Edinburg TX: meet hiring managers, submit applications in person, interview onsite, and for select positions receive an offer the same day. No registration, no invitation, no fee — bring a resume.
facts: The fair is held in McAllen; the facility is Moore Air Base in Edinburg, roughly 20 miles north, and Edinburg is the city the announcements are filed under. APHIS's own job link filters USAJOBS on Edinburg with a 25-mile radius. Searching McAllen returns nothing and reads as 'not posted yet'.
USDA's 10 November press release puts the hiring at 228 positions. APHIS's hiring page describes it as hundreds of professionals across multiple career fields and previews 26 sample titles.

Of the 26 previewed titles, 11 sit under skilled trades, craft and labor: maintenance mechanic, water treatment plant operator, insect production worker, laborer, laundry technician among them. The rest cover IT specialist and IT project manager, safety and occupational health, occupational health nurse, biological science lab technician, and management and program analyst.
Applications went live on USAJOBS on 10 November, a week before the fair. Applying online in advance is what schedules an interview; walking in without applying means the standby queue.
17 to 19 November 2026, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM Central each day, Embassy Suites by Hilton McAllen Convention Center, 800 Convention Center Blvd., McAllen TX 78501.

These are competitive-service federal announcements, so each one carries its own 'This job is open to' block naming its hiring paths. Veteran, military spouse and Schedule A eligibility is decided per announcement, not by the program — read that block rather than assuming it applies.

The first sterile fly production facility in the United States, opening spring 2027 with construction finishing April 2027. Targeted at roughly 100 million sterile flies a week in 2027 and about 300 million at full capacity, to keep New World screwworm out of US livestock. The jobs are permanent federal positions standing up a facility that does not exist yet.

entries.org: Veteran Spouse Network — Coffee Chat (UT Austin)
entries.what: A free weekly virtual peer-support hour for military and veteran spouses, partners, family members and caregivers, run every Friday 1:00–2:00 PM Central by the Veteran Spouse Network. Peer-led, no presentation, no obligation to speak — drop in with a drink. Part of a wider programme that also includes the Veteran Spouse Resiliency Group, VSN Social Club, EmpowerEd and Peer 2 Peer Connect.
facts: 1:00–2:00 PM Central, 2:00–3:00 PM Eastern, virtual, free. Sessions listed through 18 December 2026 and continuing. Missing one costs nothing; the next is seven days out.

Their FAQ states you must register at least 72 hours before an event, so the cutoff is the Tuesday before a Friday session. The Zoom link arrives in the confirmation email. They also note that anyone joining more than 15 minutes late may not be admitted.

Published eligibility covers spouses and partners of active-duty members and post-service veterans, family members and caregivers of the same, and divorcees and widows or widowers of active-duty members and veterans. Most spouse programmes gate on being currently married; this one does not. Eligibility varies by session, so check the specific listing.

Housed in the Institute for Military & Veteran Family Wellness at the University of Texas at Austin, with the Steve Hicks School of Social Work and Dell Medical School. Founded January 2015 with PCORI funding. Over 800 members. Sessions facilitated by peer leaders with military or veteran backgrounds.

The network was built for Texas and is still based there, but nothing in the published eligibility names a state and the sessions are virtual. Not confirmed either way for out-of-state attendance — vsn@austin.utexas.edu is the address to settle it before registering.

entries.org: Miles for Military — free flights for junior enlisted
entries.what: A nonprofit that gives active-duty junior enlisted service members a free round-trip flight after 25 verified volunteer hours. No financial hardship required, no blackout dates, any duty station in the world to any US state or territory. Close to 2,000 flights provided and over 100,000 volunteer hours logged.
facts: Applications must go in at least 30 days ahead of the requested travel dates. For Christmas Day travel that means applying around 25 November. Short-notice requests tied to TDY, PCS, deployment or official orders may be considered case by case. This lead time is absent from almost everything circulating about the programme and it is what decides whether someone gets home.

All six branches — Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard, Space Force. National Guard and Reserve are not eligible at this time. Spouses, children and other dependents do not receive their own tickets. Financial need is not required and is not assessed.

At least 25 volunteer hours completed within the 12 months before the requested flight. Any 501(c)(3), community organisation or on-base programme counts, and hours from several organisations can be combined. A volunteer coordinator's name, phone and email is required and the hours are verified before any travel is booked.
One round trip per calendar year, and each subsequent flight requires a fresh set of 25 qualifying hours inside the preceding 12 months.
The cap cannot be topped up

$1,000 for domestic round trips, $1,500 for international. If the fare exceeds the cap the programme cannot cover the difference AND the member is not permitted to pay it themselves — the fix is different dates or a different airport. Baggage, seat upgrades, wifi and food are the member's own cost, and tickets bought before approval are not reimbursed.

An LES issued within the last 30 days showing name and pay grade, with SSN and bank details redacted; DoD ID number, branch, grade and base; the commanding officer or NCO's official .mil email; an emergency contact; volunteer coordinator details and total hours; travel dates entered as airport codes rather than names; and leave approved or coordinated. One application only — they make contact before booking.

ACT Now Education's Weekly Rundown on Saturday 21 November 2026, 1:00 PM Eastern, free and virtual, featured Jacob Cool of Miles for Military. The session also walked through ACT Now's own free resources: the Career Compass platform, certification pathways including Security+, PMP, SHRM and Scrum, Google, IBM and Splunk learning, and 12,000+ Coursera courses.

entries.org: Data Center Operations Technician program (Service to Success, VA)
entries.what: A paid four-week classroom program at NOVA's Woodbridge campus — 120 instructional hours, with limited attendance at Loudoun — followed by roughly five months of on-the-job training, paid at $28/hour throughout, leading to possible full-time Electrical Operations Technician employment. No prior data center experience required. Target start 15 February 2027, work primarily in Louisa and Fredericksburg, Virginia.
facts: $28/hour across both the four-week classroom block and the ~5 months of on-the-job training that follow. Paid training with no prior experience required is rare enough in this field to be the headline.

Screening is on mechanical aptitude, technical curiosity, reliability and interest in electrical and mechanical systems. Prior data center experience is explicitly not required — military maintenance, switchgear, plant watch and shipboard engineering backgrounds map directly onto what they are asking for.

Classroom at NOVA Woodbridge; work primarily in Louisa and Fredericksburg. Fredericksburg is roughly 25 miles from Woodbridge, Louisa roughly 75. Four weeks commuting one direction, then a posting somewhere else — a planning fact, not a disqualifier.

The material promises 'opportunity for full-time employment based on performance and successful program completion' but does not name the hiring company. Worth establishing before committing six months.

Their own site describes them as a technical recruiting and marketing firm connecting professionals with employers — not a nonprofit veteran service organisation and not a school. They are the front door for this program, so questions go to them.

NOVA's published data center offerings are a one-year Career Studies Certificate and a two-year AAS specialisation, both at Loudoun. This four-week cohort does not appear in that catalogue, so ask what, if anything, transcripts or carries a credential at the end.
The start date is given as a target rather than a commitment and no closing date for applications is published. Re-check before relying on the February date.

The QR on the posting resolves to a monday.com intake form rather than a company careers page, which is consistent with a recruiting firm running the front door: https://forms.monday.com/forms/92b181caf7b96258e1a3327a03646b4a?r=use1

entries.org: Goldman Sachs Ayco — Regional Insight Days
entries.what: In-person insight days at Goldman Sachs Ayco regional offices for second-year undergraduates: workshops, an introduction to the Ayco business and its leadership, a look at internship opportunities across Ayco, and time with the people doing the work. Applicants choose the location nearest their school or home and indicate a preferred internship office in the same application.
facts: Applications close before any of the events run. Selected participants are notified with final event details afterwards.
Morristown NJ on 7 January; Cohoes NY, Newport Beach CA and Deerfield IL all on 28 January; Dallas TX on 29 January 2027.
Must be a second-year undergraduate graduating by June 2029. Narrow for a veteran audience, but it fits student veterans on the GI Bill, military children and spouses who are sophomores now.

Goldman Sachs Ayco is workplace financial planning — a 'personal CFO' service covering benefits and equity compensation, retirement, cash flow, investments, estate planning, tax, risk and insurance for executives and employees of large companies. Goldman acquired the business in 2003. The regional offices, Cohoes NY among them, are planning operations rather than a Manhattan desk.

Whether the day is paid, whether travel is covered, and whether attending leads to internship consideration rather than being purely an introduction. None of the three appears in the material or on Goldman's own student pages, which say such programmes 'prepare' participants without promising consideration. Ask before applying.
The code on the circulating material decodes to exactly the Avature registration URL given alongside it — no discrepancy.

entries.org: Harvard Kennedy School — American Service Fellowship
entries.what: A $100,000 scholarship covering full tuition, all fees and a partial living stipend for the one-year, full-time, on-campus Mid-Career Master in Public Administration at Harvard Kennedy School. At least 50 awards, funded by roughly $5 million in private philanthropy — the largest single-year scholarship programme in HKS history. No GRE or GMAT required, application fee waived, decisions in mid-March.
facts: Admission 1 December 2026 at 12 p.m. ET; financial aid 15 January 2027 at 12 p.m. ET. Not 11:59 p.m. Every comparable deadline a candidate has met closes at midnight, which makes this the single most expensive wrong assumption available on this listing.

Material in circulation states that half the fellowships go to the military. HKS's own announcement says 'We anticipate that approximately half of the fellows will come from military service' — an expectation, not a quota and not a reserved share. The Harvard Crimson confirms the figure was a projection at launch and that no actual breakdown has been published. Never state it as a guarantee.

Plus a bachelor's degree. Qualifying service falls in three buckets: the armed forces, including active duty and veterans; federal, state, local or tribal government, which covers teachers, firefighters and law enforcement; and Peace Corps, AmeriCorps or similar full-time civilian national service.
One year in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Applicants in the Public Leadership Credential pathway or enrolled part-time are not eligible.

HKS's ten-year strategic plan credits this fellowship with a 235% increase in domestic applications to the mid-career programme. The odds are worse than at launch — an argument for applying in the current cycle rather than waiting.

What happens to remaining Post-9/11 entitlement when tuition is already fully covered is not addressed anywhere in the published material. Candidates should ask HKS financial aid directly before the deadline; whether entitlement is preserved, stacked or wasted changes the value of the award.

entries.org: Veterans Beekeeping School — Central Ohio (COBA / OSU Extension)
entries.what: A free two-year beekeeping school for honorably discharged veterans living in fifteen Central Ohio counties, taught by working beekeepers from the Central Ohio Beekeepers Association and hosted with OSU Extension. Year One is classroom plus apiary training; graduates receive a hive, a bee package, woodenware, smoker, hive tool, mite test kit and feeder in April 2028, with an assigned mentor to help set it up. Cohort 5.
facts: Material in circulation gives 4 February 2027; the programme's own page gives 6 February 2027. Applying by the 4th satisfies both. Interviews are in person on 20 February 2027.

Delaware, Fairfield, Fayette, Franklin, Hocking, Knox, Licking, Logan, Madison, Marion, Morrow, Perry, Pickaway, Ross and Union. Residency in one of them is required and the county list was behind a 'see the website' line on circulating material.

The programme page says 20 veterans will be selected for Cohort 5, with 30 applicants chosen for in-person interviews. Circulating material says 25 participants; the operator's own page is the one the application lives on.

Three required Saturday classroom sessions — 13, 20 and 27 March 2027, 9 AM to 1 PM, at the Kunz-Brundige OSU Franklin County Extension building in Columbus. Then roughly 30 hands-on apiary sessions from late April to late September, most Wednesday evenings 6 to 8 PM with some Tuesdays and weekends. Completion requires all three indoor and 18 outdoor sessions.
Classes, training, bees, woodenware and tools are free. Participants must supply their own veiled bee jacket, about $100, and scholarships for it are available on request.
You need space for a hive
In Year Two the hive is set up at the participant's own apiary. Space to keep bees is an unstated prerequisite worth planning for before applying.
Honorable discharge required, with the DD-214 shown at the in-person interview.

Claudia Khourey-Bowers, COBA vice president and a founder of the school: 330-353-2315, claudiakhoureybowers@gmail.com. First cohort ran in 2023; graduates now sit on COBA's board and the stated goal is for the school to become entirely veteran-run.

entries.org: VA Community Employment Coordinator — American Job Center, Lincoln NE
entries.what: Free one-to-one sessions with Jennifer (also listed as Jennie) Hovey, the VA Community Employment Coordinator for the Nebraska / Western Iowa Health Care System: job search and career help, applications and résumés, coordination with VA homeless services and housing resources, and referrals into local community organisations. Held in the Yutan interview room at the American Job Center of Lancaster and Saunders Counties, 1330 N Street, Suite A, Lincoln NE 68508.
facts: The American Job Center's own event listing describes this as running 'Tuesday's from 8:00am - Noon'. Circulating material presents single dates such as 24 November 2026 as standalone events, which makes a standing weekly service look like a deadline.

The AJC staff directory lists her under 'Partners Available by Appointment' rather than as on-site staff, and the event listing says appointments are made by calling 402-676-7319. Walking in cold risks a wasted trip.
Her VA email works any day
jennifer.hovey@va.gov, from VA's own Community Employment Coordinator contact list. Useful when Tuesday mornings are not possible.

Working out of the same building and absent from all circulating material: Owen Schuette, Disabled Veterans' Outreach Program and Local Veterans' Employment Representative, 402-471-2278; Andrew Strasburg, Veteran Job-Seeker Services, 402-471-4477; Matthew Davis, Veteran's Reemployment Coordinator, 402-471-9915. The DVOP role exists for veterans with significant barriers to employment. Main center line 402-441-1640.

The VA's link between veterans and local employers and workforce services. The role sits inside VA's homeless programs structure — structure, not a gate: nothing in the listing restricts the outreach to veterans who are homeless, and framing it that way would stop the people who need it from attending.
CECs are a national VA programme and every American Job Center has veteran representatives. Outside Nebraska the transferable move is to ask the local center for the CEC and the DVOP by title.

entries.org: Service to Success — SkillBridge job board
entries.what: A technical recruiting firm's board of DoD SkillBridge placements with its industry partners, in tech, data and engineering. Roles listed on 23 November 2026: Network Test Lab Engineer (Roseville CA hybrid or Andover MA); Junior Data Engineer (Cincinnati OH, major US bank, up to $90K after); Data / Product Analyst (Atlanta GA, Fortune 500 aviation, $90–120K on completion).
facts: Industry partners are not permitted to pay SkillBridge participants. DoD continues the member's salary, allowances and benefits for the duration, and the host cannot pay a wage, salary or stipend for SkillBridge time. Any hourly or annual figure on a SkillBridge listing is what the role pays IF hired afterwards. Circulating material put '$35-40/hr (~$73-94k/yr)' under a SKILLBRIDGE badge with no 'after' qualifier, which reads as pay during the placement. This recurs on nearly every SkillBridge flyer — check it every time.
Completing a SkillBridge placement does not entitle the participant to employment with the host. Conversion happens but is earned during the placement, not promised at the start.
180 continuous days of active duty must already be completed before starting, and participation must fall inside the final 180 days before separation or retirement.

Approval comes from the first field-grade commander in the chain with Article 15 authority. SkillBridge is permissive duty, so it can be denied or terminated early for operational need. Start that conversation before committing to a listing.
DoD allows up to 180 days but each service sets its own caps by rank — for the Army, E-1 to E-5 get 120 days and E-8 and above get 60. Check the current cap for your own branch and paygrade.

Service to Success describes itself as a technical recruiting and marketing firm connecting professionals with employers, not a nonprofit or a school. See the separate entry for their Data Center Operations Technician program.

entries.what: A free weekly live session from ACT Now Education on Zoom, open to the military community, pairing an outside speaker with a walk through ACT Now's own free resources — the Career Compass platform, certification pathways including Security+, PMP, SHRM and Scrum, Google, IBM and Splunk learning, and 12,000+ Coursera courses.
facts: Runs on Saturdays, 1:00 PM Eastern, live on Zoom, free. Registration and the current schedule sit at actnoweducation.org/weekly-rundown, which is also exactly where the flyer QR resolves.

ACT Now ran two free AI sessions on Saturday 28 November 2026, five hours apart and aimed at different audiences. 1:00 PM ET, the Weekly Rundown with Michael Wish of White Feather AI on building a personal AI agent for your own email, calendar and task list. 6:00 PM ET, a live demo with Robbe Addis of Ready Waypoint on AI for business owners — morning brief, drafted replies, follow-ups sorted by urgency — hosted with Jai Salters and Nicole Dhanraj. Registration for the 6 PM session was a direct Zoom link: us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/A1Mb8qPTSmKNKRSbNW5WvA

An agent that manages mail and calendar needs a real permission grant to those accounts. For active duty, DoD civilians, contractors and cleared personnel, connecting a third-party AI tool to a work or .mil account is very likely against policy and can be a reportable incident. Use a personal account, grant read and draft before send, and check the organisation's own AI policy first. This applies to every AI-agent session, not just this one.

Michael Wish runs White Feather AI, which trains veterans and first responders on AI. Skool community of roughly 417 members; published pitch is a first AI-driven income stream within 45 days. The community lists as free but reviewers describe themselves as paying members, so pricing is unclear from outside. The Rundown session itself is free and hosted by ACT Now.
21 November 2026 featured Jacob Cool of Miles for Military on volunteering — see the separate Miles for Military entry for the free flights programme behind it.

Searches on 26 November returned several similarly named AI firms and none that confirm this one; Robbe Addis's LinkedIn is not fetchable. He is named here as the presenter because the host says so — nothing beyond that is established.

entries.org: ACT Now Education — 10 benefits for military families
entries.what: A ten-resource card from ACT Now Education covering free vehicles, flights, hotel points, hotel stays, business and certification training, professional clothing, a children's summer camp and family retreats. All ten QR codes on the card were decoded and every destination opened and read on 27 November 2026. Eight are accurate as printed; two carry conditions the card does not state and one link circulates in two different forms.
facts: The 100,000 Hilton Honors points figure is a lifetime maximum per person, not an annual allowance. Only 33 states participate and each sets its own rules. Applications go through a veterans representative at an American Job Center, or HiltonHonors@naswa.org — not through Hilton directly. Covers job-interview and training travel. Does NOT cover conferences, career fairs, general job searching, relocation or house hunting. Active duty are generally ineligible unless transitioning. naswa.org/partnerships/hilton-honors

Keys to Progress 2026 is closed for all three categories. Progressive's own page says to check back later for 2027 application timelines — no window has been published anywhere. Any specific 2027 date in circulation did not come from Progressive. progressive.com/about/purpose/keys-to-progress/

The card's QR resolves to militaryonesource.mil/mwr-digital-library, which is the official front door and where sign-in works. Other copies of this list circulate dodmwrlibraries.org instead. Use the Military OneSource address.

The National Military Family Association's own page describes free weeklong summer camp experiences and does not mention any fee. The card prints a $25 refundable deposit. Both may hold depending on site and year — confirm at registration. Travel to camp is not covered. militaryfamily.org/programs/operation-purple/operation-purple-camp/

Willing Warriors serves wounded, ill and injured service members and their families, and the programme is built around military hospitals in the National Capital Region. Their page states neither weeklong, nor six-day, nor free. Not advertised as a general veteran benefit. willingwarriors.org/warrior-retreat

Operation Homefront (operationhomefront.org/our-programs/), Fisher House (fisherhouse.org/programs/), EBV at Syracuse IVMF (ivmf.syracuse.edu/ebv), Save A Suit (saveasuit.org/requestasuit/) and Onward to Opportunity (ivmf.syracuse.edu/programs/o2o) all resolve to live pages with current intake and nothing on the card misstates them. EBV requires a post-9/11 service-connected disability; Save A Suit works on demonstrated need and stock on hand.
Every QR on the card was decoded on 27 November 2026 and each destination opened. No code is dead and none redirects somewhere unexpected.
